import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Set a clean theme for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", rc={"axes.facecolor": ".95"})

# Define a logical order for BMI Category for better visualization
bmi_order = ['Normal Weight', 'Normal', 'Overweight', 'Obese']
df['BMI Category'] = pd.Categorical(df['BMI Category'], categories=bmi_order, ordered=True)

# Create an insightful relplot to visualize the relationships
# - X-axis: Sleep Duration
# - Y-axis: Quality of Sleep
# - Hue (color): Stress Level, showing how stress impacts sleep patterns
# - Size: Daily Steps, indicating physical activity level
# - Columns (faceting): BMI Category, to see how these relationships differ across BMI groups
g = sns.relplot(
    data=df,
    x="Sleep Duration",
    y="Quality of Sleep",
    hue="Stress Level",
    size="Daily Steps",
    col="BMI Category",
    col_wrap=2,  # Arrange facets in 2 columns for a compact layout (assuming 4 BMI categories)
    palette="viridis",  # A sequential color palette suitable for stress level
    sizes=(50, 600),  # Range of point sizes for Daily Steps
    alpha=0.7,  # Transparency for better visibility of overlapping points
    height=4.5,  # Height of each facet
    aspect=1.2,  # Aspect ratio of each facet
    linewidth=0,  # No line around points
    marker='o'  # Explicitly set marker style
)

# Set a descriptive common title for the entire figure
g.fig.suptitle('Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep by Stress Level and BMI Category', y=1.03, fontsize=16)

# Adjust subplot titles to be more readable
g.set_titles("BMI: {col_name}")

# Set clear axis labels
g.set_axis_labels("Sleep Duration (hours)", "Quality of Sleep (1-10)")

# Add a legend title for clarity
g.add_legend(title="Stress Level", loc='center right', bbox_to_anchor=(1.08, 0.5))

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/titles from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.98]) # Adjust rect to make space for suptitle

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
